The must-sees

6 places Wizzy will tap you for first, each with a story and something to look for.

  1. 01
    Neighbourhood

    Birgu

    The Knights made it their first base when they arrived in 1530. After the Great Siege of 1565 it was given the title Città Vittoriosa, the victorious city.

    Look for

    Find the Inquisitor’s Palace, where the Roman Inquisition in Malta held court and kept prisoners from 1574 until 1798.

  2. 02
    Fortress

    Fort St Angelo

    It was the headquarters of the Knights during the Great Siege of 1565. Under British rule it was a Royal Navy base, and part of it is still used by the Order of Malta.

  3. 03
    Fortress

    Fort St Elmo

    During the Great Siege of 1565 its small garrison held out for about a month before it fell to the Ottomans. It now houses the National War Museum, where Malta’s George Cross is displayed.

    Look for

    In the war museum, find Faith, the battered biplane fighter that helped defend Malta’s skies in 1940.

  4. 04
    Palace

    Grandmaster’s Palace

    It was the seat of the Grand Masters of the Order of St John, then of British governors. Today it houses the Office of the President of Malta and the Palace Armoury.

    Look for

    In Prince Alfred’s Courtyard, an 18th-century clock has bronze figures of Moors that strike the hours on its bells.

  5. 05
    Church · 1577

    St John’s Co-Cathedral

    Girolamo Cassar built it for the Knights of St John, and it was finished in 1577. Caravaggio’s Beheading of Saint John the Baptist, the only painting he signed, hangs in its oratory.

    Look for

    The floor is a patchwork of about 400 inlaid marble tombstones of knights, with skulls, coats of arms and Latin epitaphs.

  6. 06
    Viewpoint

    Upper Barrakka Gardens

    The gardens were laid out in the 17th century for the Italian knights of the Order. On the terrace below, the cannons of the Saluting Battery are fired every day at noon.

    Look for

    Lean over the parapet for the Three Cities across the water; to one side, a lift drops down the face of the bastion to the harbour.
